en.title: Shortest Path in a Delivery Grid
en.description:
In the grid, 1 is passable, 0 is an obstacle, and 9 is the unique destination. Starting from the top-left corner and moving between 4-directionally adjacent cells, return the minimum number of steps to reach 9; output −1 if there is no path.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains r c (1..1000), followed by r strings of length c over the characters 019; the top-left corner is passable (it may itself be 9), and there is exactly one 9.
en.explanation: Example 1: two steps down and one step right reach 9, so the answer is 3. Example 2: the start is the destination, so the answer is 0. Example 3: both exits are 0, so the answer is −1.
hints: Run BFS with a one-dimensional distance array and an index queue, entering only non-0 cells and marking each cell when it is first enqueued.
